investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent VM was never provisioned. This is an eval-detected infrastructure failure localized to the remote-agent VM scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the kata peer-pod VM on any of the 6 available nodes at the time of the eval run (2026-06-18T15:55–16:02Z). The 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had no remaining allocatable capacity ("Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm"), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable on both node sets. Because the pod never became schedulable, the agent VM was never created, and the eval runner received no evidence to satisfy the remote-agent-create contract (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState all missing). The same scheduling error reproduced identically for remote-agent-state and remote-agent-runtime, confirming the failure is at the cluster resource layer rather than in the eval runner logic itself.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1759-1764: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) which is the code path that submits the pod; the pod never returned a schedulable state so no evidence was written downstream.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all allocatable VM slots are consumed by existing workloads, leaving zero capacity for new remote-agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

Secondary — node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod spec is too restrictive: only 2 of 6 nodes are eligible for kata peer-pods, and those 2 are already at capacity. If the selector were broadened or more nodes were labeled, scheduling might succeed.

Tertiary — a concurrent workload spike or leaked/stuck remote-agent pods from a prior run consumed the remaining kata.peerpods.io/vm slots before this eval ran, leaving no headroom. The withCleanup wrapper in the runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1762) is intended to release resources, but a prior failed cleanup could leave orphaned VMs occupying slots.
Lower confidence — the eval runner itself did not fail to submit the pod; the scheduler message confirms the pod was submitted and rejected, so this is not an eval infrastructure or token/auth issue.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed available (non-zero) kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the eval run, the exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and a different scheduling or API error would need to be identified.

If the pod spec's node affinity or selector were found to be misconfigured (e.g., referencing a label that no node carries), the root cause would shift from resource exhaustion to a misconfigured selector, even if the 2 kata nodes had free capacity.
If a re-run of the eval immediately after this failure succeeded without any cluster changes, it would suggest a transient capacity spike rather than sustained exhaustion.
If the eval runner logs showed the pod was never submitted (e.g., an API auth error before pod creation), the root cause would be in the eval runner or API layer rather than the Kubernetes scheduler.

If only remote-agent-create failed while remote-agent-state and remote-agent-runtime passed, a shared scheduling resource constraint would be less likely and a check-specific configuration issue would need investigation.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on all eligible nodes before attempting remote-agent creation, and fails fast with a clear capacity-exhausted message rather than waiting for the pod scheduling timeout.
Add an orphaned-pod cleanup eval that detects and reports any remote-agent pods left in a non-terminal state from prior eval runs, to catch cases where withCleanup fails silently.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's node selector is above a minimum threshold (e.g., at least 2 nodes with available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots), alerting before capacity is fully exhausted.

Consider a latency regression eval that alerts when remote-agent pod scheduling time exceeds a warning threshold (e.g., 30s) even if the pod eventually schedules, to catch capacity pressure before it becomes a full outage.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Blocks All Remote Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required kata peer-pod VM: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both reported insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs never returned an agent, and the check produced zero evidence — leaving all four required fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) missing from the result.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster serving the production-api remote-agent workload has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource across the 2 eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable capacity exists for a new peer-pod VM at the time of the eval run. The eval probe at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1784 calls createAgent with type "remote", which requires this VM resource; because the pod remained Unschedulable for 144 seconds, the probe timed out and returned no evidence, causing the contract validation to fail on all four required fields. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage — no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: concurrent workloads or prior eval runs consumed all available peer-pod VM slots, leaving no capacity for new scheduling. Supported by the explicit 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message in all three sibling check failures (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, permanently reducing the schedulable pool to those 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes are also at VM capacity, any new remote-agent pod will always be Unschedulable until capacity is freed or more matching nodes are added.

Tertiary — transient spike in concurrent remote-agent provisioning (e.g., from other eval runs, user traffic, or CI jobs) that temporarily exhausted the 2-node pool at the time of the eval run. No historical run data is available (previousRunCount=0, lastPassingAt=null) to confirm or rule out recurrence.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If the Kubernetes nodes show available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity at the time of the next eval run and the pod still fails to schedule, the root cause is not resource exhaustion but a different scheduling constraint (e.g., a broken node affinity label or a quota policy).

Add a post-run cleanup verification eval that confirms all eval-created remote agents are deleted and their VM slots released within a defined window after each probe run, catching resource leaks before they affect subsequent runs.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent VM was never provisioned. This is an eval-detected infrastructure failure localized to the remote-agent VM scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the kata peer-pod VM on any of the 6 available nodes at the time of the eval run (2026-06-18T15:55–16:02Z). The 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had no remaining allocatable capacity ("Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm"), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable on both node sets. Because the pod never became schedulable, the agent VM was never created, and the eval runner received no evidence to satisfy the remote-agent-create contract (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState all missing). The same scheduling error reproduced identically for remote-agent-state and remote-agent-runtime, confirming the failure is at the cluster resource layer rather than in the eval runner logic itself.

failed-check.timing: status=fail latencyMs=128246, pod stuck unscheduled for 122s before the check timed out.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty — no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState was written, confirming the VM was never provisioned.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 4 required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, matching the contract defined at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 253.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical Unschedulable message, latencyMs=149430, no evidence keys — same scheduling failure on a second independent pod request.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable message, latencyMs=150015, no evidence keys — same scheduling failure on a third independent pod request.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1759-1764: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) which is the code path that submits the pod; the pod never returned a schedulable state so no evidence was written downstream.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all allocatable VM slots are consumed by existing workloads, leaving zero capacity for new remote-agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

Secondary — node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod spec is too restrictive: only 2 of 6 nodes are eligible for kata peer-pods, and those 2 are already at capacity. If the selector were broadened or more nodes were labeled, scheduling might succeed.

Tertiary — a concurrent workload spike or leaked/stuck remote-agent pods from a prior run consumed the remaining kata.peerpods.io/vm slots before this eval ran, leaving no headroom. The withCleanup wrapper in the runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1762) is intended to release resources, but a prior failed cleanup could leave orphaned VMs occupying slots.
Lower confidence — the eval runner itself did not fail to submit the pod; the scheduler message confirms the pod was submitted and rejected, so this is not an eval infrastructure or token/auth issue.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed available (non-zero) kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the eval run, the exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and a different scheduling or API error would need to be identified.

If the pod spec's node affinity or selector were found to be misconfigured (e.g., referencing a label that no node carries), the root cause would shift from resource exhaustion to a misconfigured selector, even if the 2 kata nodes had free capacity.
If a re-run of the eval immediately after this failure succeeded without any cluster changes, it would suggest a transient capacity spike rather than sustained exhaustion.
If the eval runner logs showed the pod was never submitted (e.g., an API auth error before pod creation), the root cause would be in the eval runner or API layer rather than the Kubernetes scheduler.

If only remote-agent-create failed while remote-agent-state and remote-agent-runtime passed, a shared scheduling resource constraint would be less likely and a check-specific configuration issue would need investigation.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on all eligible nodes before attempting remote-agent creation, and fails fast with a clear capacity-exhausted message rather than waiting for the pod scheduling timeout.
Add an orphaned-pod cleanup eval that detects and reports any remote-agent pods left in a non-terminal state from prior eval runs, to catch cases where withCleanup fails silently.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's node selector is above a minimum threshold (e.g., at least 2 nodes with available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots), alerting before capacity is fully exhausted.

Consider a latency regression eval that alerts when remote-agent pod scheduling time exceeds a warning threshold (e.g., 30s) even if the pod eventually schedules, to catch capacity pressure before it becomes a full outage.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Blocks All Remote Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required kata peer-pod VM: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both reported insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs never returned an agent, and the check produced zero evidence — leaving all four required fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) missing from the result.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster serving the production-api remote-agent workload has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource across the 2 eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable capacity exists for a new peer-pod VM at the time of the eval run. The eval probe at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1784 calls createAgent with type "remote", which requires this VM resource; because the pod remained Unschedulable for 144 seconds, the probe timed out and returned no evidence, causing the contract validation to fail on all four required fields. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage — no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

If those 2 nodes are also at VM capacity, any new remote-agent pod will always be Unschedulable until capacity is freed or more matching nodes are added.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: those nodes are not labeled or tainted to accept remote-agent pods, so even if VM capacity existed there, pods could not be placed, leaving zero schedulable nodes.
Tertiary — concurrent or leaked agent pods consuming all VM slots: if prior eval runs or user workloads did not release kata VM resources, the pool could be fully occupied at eval time.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A successful re-run of the remote-agent-runtime probe that produces a scheduled pod and returns all five required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) would disprove that VM capacity is currently exhausted.
kubectl describe node output showing available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots greater than zero on the affinity-matching nodes would disprove resource exhaustion as the cause.
A scheduler event showing a different rejection reason (e.g., image pull failure, OOM, network policy) would indicate the VM capacity message was transient and a different root cause applies.
Evidence that the pod affinity/selector was recently changed to exclude previously eligible nodes would shift the primary cause from resource exhaustion to misconfiguration.

A passing run of sibling checks remote-agent-create or remote-agent-state while remote-agent-runtime still fails would disprove the shared-infrastructure hypothesis and localize the failure to the runtime probe specifically.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity across all affinity-matching nodes before attempting agent pod creation, surfacing resource exhaustion as a distinct check status rather than a timeout.
Add a stale-pod detection eval that lists remote-agent pods older than a configurable TTL and fails if any are found, catching cleanup failures before they exhaust VM capacity.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies at least N nodes match the remote-agent pod selector and have non-zero kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, alerting on pool shrinkage before it causes scheduling failures.

Introduce a historical baseline for the remote-agent-runtime check so that regressions from a passing state are immediately flagged (verifierContext.history shows previousRunCount=0 and lastPassingAt=null, meaning no baseline exists yet).
